newsitem.title: USA: CBOT rice ends higher after March expiry.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rice ends higher after March expiry.

text.p: CBOT rice futures rallied after the March expiry to close higher on commercial buying, traders said.
"Now that the spot month is off the board, we're trading futures again," a floor source said. "The March converged with cash and that's why it ended so much lower.
The March contract dropped 23 cents per cwt to settle at $11.50. Expiry was at 1201 CST. Trade sources said LFG, Dean Witter and E.D. and F. Man International were sellers.
The May contract gained light support from ideas Costa Rica would purchase U.S. rice.
Results of Costa Rica's 30,000-tonne tender were expected late Wednesday.
Locals were said to be sellers on the day while commercials were active buyers of new crop months.
Rice ended six cents to one cent per cwt higher with May up one at $11.62.
Volume was estimated by CBOT at 400 lots, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 284 lots.
